messages:
Alice: Quick sync — we need to pick what goes into the next micro-sprint from the bug queue.
Bob: Brief: critical search crash reported by two customers vs a few small UX polishes. Thoughts? :thinking:
Charlie: Crash looks repro-able on v2.2 when query contains emojis. Stacktrace attached earlier.
Dev1: I can take the crash but it's ~2 dev-weeks to fully refactor. Any lighter options?
PM1: Options: A) Hotfix patch (canary) to mitigate immediate crash. B) Full refactor (longer) and delay other work.
Alice: My proposal: split — immediate band-aid via hotfix/canary to stop crashes, schedule polish/refactor as a follow-on milestone.
Bob: Agree. Who will own the canary and rollout? @DevLead?
DevLead: I can own it. Need QA and eng-sre window. ETA: 48h to PR + 24h for canary observation.
QA: I can run smoke tests once PR hits canary. Acceptance criteria: crash repro rate -> 0, no perf regress >10%.
PM2: I'll draft a brief customer comms and add a maintenance note if we need a short window.
Charlie: Add a follow-on milestone for the UX polish in sprint+1. Label it "follow-on:polish" and estimate 3d.
Alice: Decision recap: take crash now via hotfix. Owner: DevLead. QA: assigned. PM: PM2 handles comms. Follow-on: polish next sprint.
DevLead: Opening PR now: branch `hotfix/crash-search`, link: https://github.com/redwood/hotfix/123 (wip)
Bob: Update backlog: move polish task to "backlog -> follow-on" and include the customer examples that showed the crash.
Alice: @eng-sre-bot can you schedule a canary window once PR merges?
eng-sre-bot: Canary scheduled for 2024-05-22T02:00Z for service "search-inference". Monitoring hooks enabled.
DevLead: PR merged to canary, starting rollout.
QA: Canary smoke passed after first checks. Running deeper validation now.
QA: Good news — crash rate dropped from 0.7% -> 0.05% in the first 2 hours. No new regressions observed.
PM2: I'll send the customer update tomorrow morning and link the mitigation notes.
Alice: Thanks everyone. Closing this thread — hotfix applied, monitoring in place, polish queued as follow-on. :raised_hands:
